title: Where Did Amelia Earhart Go? The Last Radio Line and an Island
description:
On July 2, 1937, Itasca received Amelia Earhart's last confirmed radio transmission: 'We are on the line 157/337.' It was a line of position, not her aircraft's final coordinates.

Using a 1937 Navy search report, a 1940 telegram from the island, a 1941 medical report, and later research, this episode examines two explanations: a crash near Howland Island or the Nikumaroro Island hypothesis. A deep-sea sonar target near Howland announced in 2024 was later identified as a rock. The Taraia anomaly in Nikumaroro's lagoon is a separate target that still awaits on-site identification.

Sources checked through 2026-10-15. The latest Purdue University field update available at the time is dated 2026-10-14: the team viewed Taraia with a drone and began surveying the lagoon with a magnetometer and side-scan sonar. The data await analysis, and no identification of the object has been announced. If the expedition reports new findings before publication, we will recheck and update this description.

The AI illustrations in this video are narrative reconstructions, not archival photographs, archaeological finds, or a confirmed crash site. Historical figures appear as nonportrait cartoon characters.

chapters.captain-after-silence: The Captain Maps the Last Line
chapters.lagoon-anomaly: A Lagoon Image Spurs a Search

h035intd.text: On July 2, 1937, the patrol cutter Itasca waited off Howland Island for a plane.

h1swy0kc.text: At 7:42, Earhart radioed that she could not see land and was running low on fuel.

h0qr8dzv.text: An hour later came her last confirmed radio transmission.

h1h02lye.text: At 8:43, she said, 'We are on the line 157/337.'

h1j5wr9p.text: After that, Itasca received no more transmissions confirmed as hers.

h0ac4220.text: Days later, other stations claimed possible signals. Were any reliable?

h07qifh3.text: What did the search plane see over an island to the southeast?

h1xsq9te.text: Three years later, that island sent a telegram about bones. What would a doctor say?

h1qqjkjd.text: Where did she fly last? Start with the line in the captain's hands.

h07ur373.text: The voice faded. The captain had to choose how to use that line.

h1qcc49q.text: He later wrote that the last signal was strong; hearing her did not reveal where the plane was.

h1ja5ezp.text: She and navigator Noonan had flown the Electra from Lae, New Guinea, bound for Howland Island.

h12e8tp0.text: Her 'fuel is running low' became 'half an hour left'; the original message gave no figure.

h0qvh1pv.text: The cutter heard her voice but never established full two-way contact.

h09zkgf6.text: The captain took her two bearings as a line of position based on the sun.

h039rbjd.text: The opposite bearings ran northwest and southeast, but did not tell the crew where on the line she was.

h1leys7s.text: She said she searched north and south along it, but gave no point to fix it on a map.

h0jau8g7.text: Searchers had two directions, but neither end proved the route she actually flew.

h1gc9lwh.text: The captain had to choose which end to search then, with no time for later debates.

h1piej9y.text: Itasca first searched near Howland Island; the Navy then expanded the search.

h0g8ucsn.text: The ship plotted tracks at sea; planes checked different directions for the Electra.

h1icywk8.text: Over the next 16 days, ships and planes searched more than 250,000 square miles.

h0bbh0qp.text: The possible signals also changed ships' search routes.

h0idnq0q.text: But the Navy later ruled those signals unreliable as distress calls.

h11wot3g.text: Lexington's planes searched northwest of Howland Island.

h1g85jc5.text: On July 9, Colorado's search planes flew over Gardner Island.

h1nac8m6.text: Today, that island is called Nikumaroro.

h1d4moak.text: The plane from our opening did not find either missing aviator.

h1atvqwr.text: The Navy captain's formal report saw no homes or signs of habitation.

h0txz5m2.text: But TIGHAR later transcribed a pilot's letter describing what looked like signs of recent human presence.

h0mvsgc1.text: The report's 'recent habitation' referred to Sydney Island.

h1txac5k.text: The two texts differ, but neither locates Earhart.

h1rbopkn.text: The search ended July 18, with neither aviator nor the plane found.

h021lww6.text: The Navy deemed a sea crash within about 200 miles of Howland likely.

h03v2ht9.text: That was an inference from the search, with no wreck to check.

h1awkdms.text: The search area shows its scale, not that every patch of sea was seen;

h1b6jzbr.text: it cannot pinpoint a wreck on the seabed.

h0td0us5.text: Three years later, a work party found incomplete human remains on Gardner Island.

h0k1r2r4.text: Gallagher, a colonial officer, telegrammed the find that September.

h0hg5g67.text: It also mentioned parts of a shoe, a bottle, and a sextant box.

h1j3jy6q.text: TIGHAR later published transcripts and scans of these colonial documents.

h1c1d8wp.text: Gallagher wrote that the bones 'might' be linked to Earhart.

h0ch49hg.text: The next telegram clarified: they had not found a complete skeleton.

h00ychib.text: Only part of a shoe sole remained; officials guessed it might have belonged to a woman.

h12n9upy.text: But the sole, the bottle, and the box alone could not identify their owner.

h14gqfn1.text: Gardner Island is about 650 km southeast of Howland, across another sea.

h15ef5db.text: Island-theory supporters extended the final position line toward it.

h08hfn5s.text: The bones then went to Fiji for a doctor's examination.

h0hspf6t.text: The telegram's 'might' now faced its first formal medical report.

h0ouw4gu.text: The report came the next year, and its first answer challenged the island theory.

h0bn6oho.text: By April 1941, the bones in the opening telegram reached Dr. Hoodless in Fiji.

h1kfgii9.text: He listed 13 skeletal elements, but had less than half a complete skeleton.

h1rhn7sa.text: He judged the remains male, with an age at death of about 45 to 55.

h0pu8prr.text: He estimated 5 feet 5.5 inches tall, about 166 cm.

h0sfucco.text: He did not identify the bones as Earhart's; the telegram's 'might' remained a guess.

h11eqjzh.text: But the case was not closed: later researchers could revisit the doctor's measurements.

h0zl9z2e.text: A later paper's abstract says Cross and Wright still supported the male finding in 2015.

h1wxgntv.text: In 2018, researcher Jantz recalculated the surviving measurements.

h09f4dtw.text: He argued Earhart's measurements were closer to the bones than those of 99% of a reference sample.

h171rf4q.text: That is not a 99% chance it was her; it compares measurements with a reference sample.

h0zzkpup.text: Records do not say for certain where the bones went.

h1q8ext8.text: TIGHAR could not find them, so there are no remains to test directly for DNA.

h0o2pb8r.text: Without bones to retest, an identifiable aircraft part was still needed.

h0jsz7sj.text: In 2020, an unusual shape in imagery of Nikumaroro's lagoon drew attention.

h02x2mhu.text: ALI, the Archaeological Legacy Institute behind the search, saw possible Electra wreckage.

h1v8djl5.text: The Taraia Object lies in the island's lagoon, not deep water near Howland.

h12wdt1c.text: ALI later found images from different years and argued the same outline may have long been there.

h00s999r.text: How could a plane-like image lead to identifiable physical evidence?

h1j9uace.text: TIGHAR, long a backer of the Nikumaroro theory, offered a different reading in 2021.

h1c7nl2d.text: Its journal said discussants saw a coconut tree; TIGHAR itself said it looked like driftwood.

h0xw6uto.text: Backing the idea Earhart reached the island does not make this object her plane.

h0v92d1n.text: In 2024, another team released a plane-like deep-sea sonar image near Howland.

h10nc5h1.text: Later that year, it said the target it had pursued was just a natural rock.

h17piur2.text: That target was elsewhere, found by another method; the rock finding cannot be applied to Taraia.

h1olfg1r.text: That false lead shows an outline seen from afar is not an identified aircraft.

h1quni8g.text: In 2026, a team finally boarded ship, ready to touch the lagoon target.

h0566j3u.text: The team reached Nikumaroro on October 12; they landed and set up the next day.

h0m234ej.text: ALI led the expedition, with Purdue University and the Purdue Research Foundation.

h0op7m6k.text: Does the lagoon anomaly contain parts identifiable as Earhart's Electra?

h1e4dxa5.text: The search began on land: on October 13, the team surveyed Taraia Peninsula's sandbar.

h031d5vr.text: On October 14, the team used a drone

h02rdk6s.text: to inspect the Taraia Object in the lagoon.

h155hpnc.text: An underwater team began magnetometer and side-scan sonar surveys;

h1lrep92.text: They plan to touch the target with a hydroprobe, checking material, edges, and shape.

h1sr7ftu.text: Only then can they compare instrument readings with the object they actually touch.

h1umhdsw.text: After recording that, they can clear the silt carefully and view the object.

h1s0vr7z.text: ALI plans to check for fuselage metal, shape, and that Electra model's rivet pattern.

h1b4z5xa.text: If it turns out to be wood, this suspect target can be ruled out.

h142sgn9.text: If plane parts appear, they must check if they are from her Electra.

h1mph050.text: ALI's plan says ruling out an aircraft would still complete the identification.

h0c0hnrn.text: Ruling out this island object would not prove the Navy's proposed crash site.

h0ctdw9q.text: As of October 14, no wreckage has been confirmed as part of that Electra. Earhart's final route remains unresolved.

h0tcwx67.text: If you could follow one lead, would it be the radio call or the lagoon object?

h1vh1gxs.text: Subscribe to our channel and follow the records with us to the clearest view of this mystery.
